added_items.item: Set maxmemory-policy noeviction on Redis, otherwise queue keys can be evicted when memory is full, which silently loses jobs
Postgres queue risks: extra write load and table bloat on the main DB, which can slow app queries. Mitigate with frequent vacuum, deleting old completed jobs, or a separate database
Redis persistence can lose jobs with periodic snapshots as well as with persistence off, so enable AOF
Postgres polling adds latency; pg-boss and graphile-worker mitigate it with LISTEN/NOTIFY
Failed jobs, retries and history are easy to inspect with plain SQL
SKIP LOCKED lets many workers claim jobs without blocking each other
BullMQ has a good dashboard ecosystem and mature features: delayed jobs, priorities, repeatable jobs
Redis is a second system to host and secure
Decision checklist, including the transactional enqueue example (create user and queue welcome email atomically)
Set maxmemory-policy noeviction on Redis, otherwise Redis can evict queue keys when memory is full (job loss)
Postgres queues add write load and table bloat on the main DB; heavy traffic can slow app queries; mitigate with frequent vacuum, deleting old completed jobs, or a separate database
Redis can lose jobs on crash with persistence off or periodic snapshots (explains why AOF matters; Y only mentions AOF absence/restart)
Postgres polling adds latency; pg-boss and graphile-worker mitigate with LISTEN/NOTIFY
Postgres failed jobs, retries, and history are easy to inspect with plain SQL
BullMQ has a good dashboard ecosystem
Redis has mature features: delayed jobs, priorities, repeatable jobs (Y mentions only rate limiting and flows)
